title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 43
paragraphs: When the army had come to the river Scamander — the first of all the rivers they had reached since setting out from Sardis, whose stream failed and was not sufficient for the drinking of the army and its animals — when, I say, Xerxes came to this river, he went up to the Citadel of Priam, wishing to see it. Having viewed it and learned all its details by inquiry, he sacrificed a thousand heifers to Athena of Ilium, and the Magi poured libations in honor of the heroes. After they had done this, a panic fell upon the army in the night. At daybreak Xerxes set out from there, keeping on his left the cities of Rhoeteum, Ophryneum, and Dardanus (which borders Abydos), and on his right the Gergith Teucrians.
